questions.question: What is the N+1 query problem in ActiveRecord and how do you fix it?
questions.title: The N+1 Query Problem
questions.direct_answer: The N+1 problem is when you fetch N records and then trigger one extra query per record to load an association — 1 query for the posts plus N queries for each post's comments (N+1 total), which is slow. It happens when you call an association method on each record in a loop (post.comments inside posts.each). You fix it with eager loading: Post.includes(:comments) loads all the comments in one extra query upfront (or one JOIN), so iterating no longer fires per-row queries. Spot it in the log as repeated SELECTs on the associated table.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you can spot N+1 (one query + N per-record queries) and fix it with includes (eager loading).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Not noticing the N+1 in the log, or 'fixing' it by caching instead of eager loading.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: N+1 = 1 query for the records + N per-record association queries. Fix with Post.includes(:comments) to eager-load in one extra query.

sections.title: One Plus N Queries
sections.content: The N+1 problem is when you fetch N records and then trigger one extra query per record to load an association — 1 query for the posts plus N queries for each post's comments, N+1 total, which is slow. It happens when you call an association method on each record in a loop: post.comments inside posts.each fires a query for each post. You fix it with eager loading: Post.includes(:comments) loads all the comments in one extra query upfront (or one JOIN), so iterating no longer fires per-row queries. You spot it in the log as repeated SELECTs on the associated table — the signature of N+1.

sections.title: N+1 vs Eager Loaded
sections.content:
Without includes, each post.comments fires a query; with includes, one extra query loads them all.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph N+1
    Q1[SELECT * FROM posts] --> P1[post1.comments -> query]
    P1 --> P2[post2.comments -> query]
  end
  subgraph Fixed
    I[Post.includes\(:comments\)] --> Q2[1 query for posts + 1 for all comments]
  end
```

sections.title: N+1 and the includes fix
sections.content:
```ruby
# N+1: 1 query for posts, then N queries (one per post) for comments.
posts = Post.all
posts.each { |p| puts p.comments.count }   # N queries on comments!

# FIX: eager-load comments with includes (1 extra query for ALL comments).
posts = Post.includes(:comments)
posts.each { |p| puts p.comments.length }   # no per-post query

# In the log you'll see:
#   SELECT 'posts'.* FROM 'posts'
#   SELECT 'comments'.* FROM 'comments' WHERE 'comments'.'post_id' IN (1,2,3,...)  # one query
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Not noticing the N+1 in the log (repeated SELECTs on the associated table).
'Fixing' it by caching the association instead of eager loading (the real fix is includes).
Using includes when you don't iterate the association (unnecessary; only fix what you use).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: N+1 = 1 query for the records plus N per-record association queries (one per row).
It happens when you call an association in a loop (post.comments inside posts.each).
Fix with Post.includes(:comments) to eager-load all comments in one extra query.
Spot it in the log as repeated SELECTs on the associated table.
Only eager-load associations you actually use (don't includes everything blindly).

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: The N+1 problem is when you fetch N records and then trigger one extra query per record to load an association — one query for the posts plus N queries for each post's comments, N+1 total, which is slow. It happens when you call an association method on each record in a loop: post.comments inside posts.each fires a query for each post. You fix it with eager loading: Post.includes of comments loads all the comments in one extra query upfront, or one JOIN, so iterating no longer fires per-row queries. You spot it in the log as repeated SELECTs on the associated table, which is the signature of N+1. A common mistake is not noticing the N+1 in the log, or fixing it by caching instead of eager loading, when the real fix is includes.
